title: Evaluation Aliasing in Persistent Agent Memory

relationship_to_existing_d5.reason: The environment-order paper audits benchmark backend carryover under task permutation. This idea studies whether a finite current evaluation aliases distinct persistent memory states that later have different controlled effects. The causal variables and decisive experiments are different.

scientific_question: Can distinct persistent memories receive the same non-degenerate score signature on one common current panel while producing different controlled effects on a sealed future panel?
hypothesis: Finite current task evaluation can induce behavioral alias classes over persistent memory states: at least one class that is exactly score-equivalent on a common current panel will contain memories with different placebo-controlled future effects across multiple task families.
claim_boundary: No claim of byte-identical internal-state history effects. No claim of a new bisimulation theorem. The target is an empirical and methodological failure mode of finite evaluation for persistent agent memory.

closest_reductions: classical behavioral state abstraction and bisimulation
model-level completion-score aliasing versus state-tracking ability
novelty_state.residual: No located work first constructs exact same-current-evaluation alias classes over persistent external memories and then opens an outcome-sealed future panel to test controlled effect divergence.

current_f0.memory_pool: four heldout-candidate memories, exactly one from each frozen source family
current_f0.stage_b_open_condition: At least one size>=2 non-degenerate exact Stage-A alias class with reproducible no-memory controls.

anti_outcome_shopping: Do not replace memories after Stage-A outcomes.
Do not replace Stage-B tasks after Stage-A outcomes.
Do not reopen the superseded Qwen panel once Gemma consumes its frozen task identities.
Do not create a manuscript from Stage-A alias discovery alone.
Do not create a paper from a one-task or one-family future divergence.
